\section[dēngshān]{dēngshān — to climb a mountain}

\label{lesson:ZH-C435-dengshan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Mandarin for to keep as a souvenir, then the Mandarin for an account of a journey.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: dēngshān}
\emph{dēngshān} — \textquotedblleft{}to climb a mountain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\emph{zhōumò wǒmen zuò huǒchē qù dēngshān} — At the weekend we're taking the train to go climbing.
\end{quote}

Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dēngshān} is built from \emph{dēng} 'to ascend' and \zh{山} 'a mountain', both inherited from Middle Chinese, \emph{tong} and \emph{srean} (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'to rise' and 'to go up'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dēngshān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dēngshān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zhōumò wǒmen zuò huǒchē qù dēngshān} — At the weekend we're taking the train to go climbing.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Mandarin for to keep as a souvenir, then the Mandarin for an account of a journey, then say \emph{dēngshān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does dēngshān mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To climb a mountain\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[shāndǐng]{shāndǐng — top of a mountain; summit}

\label{lesson:ZH-C435-shanding}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Mandarin for an account of a journey, then the Mandarin for to climb a mountain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: shāndǐng}
\emph{shāndǐng} — \textquotedblleft{}top of a mountain; summit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\emph{cóng zhèr wǎng qián zǒu shí fēnzhōng jiù dào shāndǐng le} — Walk on for ten minutes from here and you'll be at the top.
\end{quote}

Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{shāndǐng} is built from \zh{山} 'a mountain' and \emph{dǐng} 'the top', both inherited from Middle Chinese, \emph{srean} and \emph{tengX} (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the second as the crown of the head.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shāndǐng}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shāndǐng}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cóng zhèr wǎng qián zǒu shí fēnzhōng jiù dào shāndǐng le} — Walk on for ten minutes from here and you'll be at the top.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Mandarin for an account of a journey, then the Mandarin for to climb a mountain, then say \emph{shāndǐng} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does shāndǐng mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Top of a mountain; summit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\zh{日出} (rìchū)}{日出 (rìchū)}]{\zh{日出} (rìchū) — sunrise}

\label{lesson:ZH-C435-richu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Mandarin for to climb a mountain, then the Mandarin for the summit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \zh{日出}}
\textbf{\zh{日出}} — \emph{rìchū} — \textquotedblleft{}sunrise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\zh{我们早上五点起来看日出}} \emph{wǒmen zǎoshang wǔ diǎn qǐlai kàn rìchū} — We're getting up at five in the morning to watch the sunrise.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\zh{日出}} (\emph{rìchū}) is built from \zh{日} 'the sun' and \zh{出} 'to come out', both inherited from Middle Chinese, \emph{nyit} and \emph{tsyhwit} (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rìchū}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rìchū}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{wǒmen zǎoshang wǔ diǎn qǐlai kàn rìchū} — We're getting up at five in the morning to watch the sunrise.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Mandarin for to climb a mountain, then the Mandarin for the summit, then say \emph{rìchū} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[zhuàngguān]{zhuàngguān — magnificent; spectacular}

\label{lesson:ZH-C435-zhuangguan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Mandarin for the summit, then the Mandarin for the sunrise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: zhuàngguān}
\emph{zhuàngguān} — \textquotedblleft{}magnificent; spectacular\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\emph{shāndǐng de rìchū hěn zhuàngguān} — The sunrise from the summit is spectacular.
\end{quote}

Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{zhuàngguān} is built from \emph{zhuàng} 'grand' and \emph{guān} 'a sight', both inherited from Middle Chinese, \emph{tsrjangH} and \emph{kwan} (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'big' and the second 'to view'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zhuàngguān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shāndǐng de rìchū hěn zhuàngguān} — The sunrise from the summit is spectacular.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Mandarin for the summit, then the Mandarin for the sunrise, then say \emph{zhuàngguān} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\zh{下山} (xiàshān)}{下山 (xiàshān)}]{\zh{下山} (xiàshān) — to come down a mountain}

\label{lesson:ZH-C435-xiashan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Mandarin for the sunrise, then the Mandarin for spectacular.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \zh{下山}}
\textbf{\zh{下山}} — \emph{xiàshān} — \textquotedblleft{}to come down a mountain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\zh{下山以后我们坐车回酒店}} \emph{xiàshān yǐhòu wǒmen zuò chē huí jiǔdiàn} — After coming down the mountain, we take the bus back to the hotel.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\zh{下山}} (\emph{xiàshān}) is built from \zh{下} 'to go down' and \zh{山} 'a mountain', both inherited from Middle Chinese, \emph{haeX} and \emph{srean} (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'low' and 'to come down'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{xiàshān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{xiàshān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{xiàshān yǐhòu wǒmen zuò chē huí jiǔdiàn} — After coming down the mountain, we take the bus back to the hotel.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Mandarin for the sunrise, then the Mandarin for spectacular, then say \emph{xiàshān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \zh{下山} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To come down a mountain\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Seeing the Sights to At the Top}

\label{lesson:ZH-R435-review-430-435}



\begin{quote}
Say the Mandarin for to go sightseeing and a historic site.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} to go sightseeing, a historic site, a scenic area, to take a selfie, the peak season
  \item \emph{Say it:} to give a running commentary, a spring outing, a pleasure boat, many, to pose for a group photo
  \item \emph{Say it:} few, the off season, a public holiday, a full-price ticket, to be shut to the public
  \item \emph{Say it:} to receive visitors, beyond the sea, a sea of people, a Chinese person settled abroad, to go out to sea
  \item \emph{Say it:} a tour group, to meet up as a group, to do some shopping, to keep as a souvenir, an account of a journey
  \item \emph{Say it:} to climb a mountain, the summit, the sunrise, spectacular, to come down a mountain
  \item \emph{Read it:} \zh{游} \zh{海} — each one aloud, then a word that holds it
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To go sightseeing? (\emph{guānguāng}.) A historic site? (\emph{gǔjì}.) A scenic area? (\emph{jǐngqū}.) To take a selfie? (\emph{zìpāi}.) The peak season? (\emph{wàngjì}.) To give a running commentary? (\textbf{\zh{解说}}, \emph{jiěshuō}.) A spring outing? (\textbf{\zh{春游}}, \emph{chūnyóu}.) A pleasure boat? (\textbf{\zh{游船}}, \emph{yóuchuán}.) Many? (\textbf{\zh{多}}, \emph{duō}.) To pose for a group photo? (\emph{héyǐng}.) Few? (\textbf{\zh{少}}, \emph{shǎo}.) The off season? (\emph{dànjì}.) A public holiday? (\textbf{\zh{节假日}}, \emph{jiéjiàrì}.) A full-price ticket? (\textbf{\zh{全票}}, \emph{quánpiào}.) To be shut to the public? (\emph{guānbì}.) To receive visitors? (\emph{jiēdài}.) Beyond the sea? (\textbf{\zh{海外}}, \emph{hǎiwài}.) A sea of people? (\textbf{\zh{人山人海}}, \emph{rénshānrénhǎi}.) A Chinese person settled abroad? (\emph{huáqiáo}.) To go out to sea? (\textbf{\zh{出海}}, \emph{chūhǎi}.) A tour group? (\emph{lǚyóutuán}.) To meet up as a group? (\emph{jíhé}.) To do some shopping? (\emph{gòuwù}.) To keep as a souvenir? (\emph{liúniàn}.) An account of a journey? (\textbf{\zh{游记}}, \emph{yóujì}.) To climb a mountain? (\emph{dēngshān}.) The summit? (\emph{shāndǐng}.) The sunrise? (\textbf{\zh{日出}}, \emph{rìchū}.) Spectacular? (\emph{zhuàngguān}.) To come down a mountain? (\textbf{\zh{下山}}, \emph{xiàshān}.)
